---
title: Sources and Tools
---

A source is a retrieval adapter. A tool is a model-visible action. Keeping them
separate lets the same corpus support search, visit, or a custom interaction
without putting model-facing schemas into the storage layer.

## Source contract

Every `DataSource` provides asynchronous `search`, `fetch`, and `close`
operations. Sources return provider-neutral `Document` and `SearchResult`
objects.

| `type` | Backend |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Full-text search and file reads under a local root; requires `rg` |
| `web` | Serper search and Jina page fetching |
| `elasticsearch` | BM25, vector, or hybrid retrieval |
| `custom` | A project-defined `DataSource` class |

Each source needs a unique name. Source-backed tools refer to these names:

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: project_docs
      root_path: ./docs
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_docs
      source: [project_docs]
    - type: visit
      name: visit_doc
      source: [project_docs]
```

## Elasticsearch retrieval

Elasticsearch supports `bm25`, `vector`, and `hybrid` search modes. Vector and
hybrid search require an embedding endpoint and a populated vector field.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: corpus
      hosts: [http://127.0.0.1:9200]
      index: documents
      search_fields: [title, text]
      title_field: title
      text_field: text
      url_field: url
      vector_search_mode: hybrid
      vector_field: text_vector
      embedding_model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
      embedding_base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8004/v1
      embedding_api_key: EMPTY
      embedding_prefix: |-
        Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query
        Query:
      es_max_concurrency: 256
      embedding_max_concurrency: 256
```

Check whether the embedding server applies query prompts automatically. Apply
`embedding_prefix` exactly once, and use the same embedding model and vector
dimension that were used to build the index.

Highlighting builds compact snippets from matching fragments. Tune fragment
size, fragment count, and `snippet_chars` against the context budget rather
than returning entire documents from search.

## Model-visible tool contract

The tool name, description, and `inputSchema` are visible to the model. The
schema should expose only arguments the model can use correctly.

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_web
      description: Search the indexed web corpus for relevant evidence.
      source: [corpus]
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          keywords:
            type: string
            description: A focused search query.
        required: [keywords]
        additionalProperties: false
      argument_mapping:
        keywords: query
      raise_argument_validation_error: false
```

`argument_mapping` translates model-visible names to implementation arguments.
When validation errors are not raised, the tool returns an actionable schema
error to the model so it can correct the call.

## Built-in tools

SearcherKit registers `search`, `visit`, `multi_source_search`,
`multi_source_visit`, and `mcp`. MCP tools share the same initialization,
validation, concurrency, and shutdown lifecycle as native tools.

Large search or visit results can be passed through a summarizer model:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [corpus]
      summary_goal_key: goal
      summarizer:
        model: Qwen3-8B
        base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1
        api_key: EMPTY
        max_chars: 40000
        max_concurrency: 128
        default_kwargs:
          max_tokens: 1024
        retry_config:
          max_tries: 3
```

Summarization reduces context growth but adds latency, cost, and another failure
boundary. Use it when documents are substantially larger than the evidence the
agent needs.
